sentences.text: Modern equipment can call for help faster than you can talk.
A VHF radio with digital selective calling has a red distress button.
Press it, and it sends an automatic alert, with your MMSI number and your GPS position, on channel seventy.
Then follow up by voice on channel sixteen.
That button only sends your position if the radio is connected to a GPS, and it only identifies you if you registered an MMSI.
An EPIRB sends a distress signal on four hundred six megahertz to satellites, which pass your identity and position to the rescuers.
It must be registered with NOAA.
A personal locator beacon does the same thing for one person, and you wear it.
And keep all of it current: the registrations, the batteries, and the hydrostatic release.
